transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-09-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Novacare Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Novacare Legal), Sana Malik (Novacare VP Eng), David Hsu (Novacare Security)
Links shared: Redwood MSA draft (link), DPA summary (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), onboarding runbook (link)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. i'm jordan from redwood, with priya and ethan on the line. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marta: doing well, thanks. we wanted to get aligned on the procurement path - msa, dpa, slas, pricing - and what you need from us.
[00:15] Jordan: perfect, that's the goal. quick agenda: review our MSA/DPA status, talk SLA tiers and latency targets, pricing model (hosted vs reserved), and then next steps for procurement and onboarding. sound good?
[00:26] Sana: yes, let's do that.

[02:10] Priya: i'll jump in on the technical side - for the onboarding options we support hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private vpc deployment. for regulated claims like yours we usually recommend private with customer-managed kms or dedicated capacity depending on traffic.
[02:30] David: on kms - we need HSM-backed keys and customer-managed keys in aws kms, ideally. also need clarity on audit logs retention, and whether payloads are persisted.
[02:45] Ethan: yeah, good q. by default hosted API logs are retained for 90 days for diagnostics, but we have an enterprise setting with longer retention and the ability to disable retention. we'll add precise docs.

[05:00] Liam: on the legal front i'm looking at the msa we received. there are a few standard redlines: indemnity cap, IP ownership for derivative prompts, and a carve-out for regulatory subpoenas. i'm also checking subprocessors in the dpa - need the full list.
[05:18] Jordan: understood. we'll send a redline version with comments. our standard is to limit indemnity and keep customer data ownership; for IP, we have a policy that customers retain rights to inputs and outputs, but model improvements are separate - we can discuss a carve-out.
[05:35] Marta: timeline - procurement wants pricing approved and PO by the 20th. is that feasible?
[05:42] Jordan: pace looks ok if legal turnaround is quick. we'll prioritize the MSA redline this week. pricing approvals - depends on model mix and whether you want reserved capacity.

[08:00] Sana: can you walk through the pricing difference between hosted and reserved? we have variable workloads; cost predictability is important.
[08:12] Priya: sure. hosted is usage-based per-token; you pay for what you use but cost can spike if traffic surges. reserved/dedicated gives a committed monthly capacity across gpu pools with a discount vs hosted and predictable unit economics. we also have autoscale burst credits for 10-20% spikes.
[08:35] Jordan: i'll attach a pricing spreadsheet with a few scenarios (baseline hosted, 6-month reserved, 12-month reserved) so your finance team can model it.

[10:20] David: SLA - what uptime and latency SLOs do you offer? our app requires 99.9% uptime for the API and 95th percentile latency under 200ms for short prompts.
[10:33] Ethan: 99.9% is our enterprise SLA for dedicated; hosted tier is typically 99.5. latency depends on model size and token length; for staging we benchmarked a trimmed open model at ~120ms p95 on dedicated gpu profiles. we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet with p50/p95 numbers.
[10:52] Sana: we need guarantees around fallbacks - if a dedicated pool is degraded, will you auto-failover to hosted? any data residency implications?
[11:02] Priya: we have smart routing policies - can failover to a compatible region or to a hosted fallback, but for private/vpc deployments that option may not be permitted. we'll document exact behavior per deployment option.

[14:40] Marta: procurement question - for the MSA, do you accept our vendor addendum? we generally prefer to keep our changes minimal but will push a couple of clauses.
[14:50] Jordan: we usually review addendums, open to negotiating. if you send it we'll map redlines against our standard and highlight any high-risk clauses.

[17:30] Liam: one quick thing on breach notification timelines - we'd like 24 hours for critical incidents. is that in your standard?
[17:40] David: yes, that's important.
[17:45] Priya: our enterprise policy is 48 hours for initial notification, full report within 30 days. we can escalate to 24 hours for contracted critical incidents subject to our incident response SLAs - i'll note that as a negotiable item.

[20:00] Jordan: i want to call out subprocessors - our infra providers include major cloud vendors and a managed logging provider. we'll provide a list and SOC2/ISO artifacts.
[20:12] David: please include the subprocessors list; we have to run them through our vendor risk tool.

[23:10] Sana: on onboarding, what's typical timeline from PO to production? we have a target of mid-october for feature launch.
[23:20] Ethan: typical is 4-6 weeks for reserved or private deployment, less for hosted. initial steps: legal signoff, finance PO, then technical kickoff to provision VPC and keys, then test harness and pilot.

[26:00] Marta: ok. we also need a billing contact and the final pricing sheet for approval. can you send an itemized quote?
[26:10] Jordan: yes - itemized quote and workbook will go out; do you have a preferred billing cadence? monthly or annual?
[26:20] Marta: monthly with option to prepay annually for discount.

[28:30] Priya: small note - for larger models we recommend quantized weights and batching configs to reduce cost. we can provide model recommendations based on latency/quality tradeoffs.
[28:45] Sana: perfect, that helps our engineering tradeoff analysis.

[31:00] Liam: on the DPA, we need clarity on data retention, right to be forgotten requests, and cross-border transfer mechanisms - are you using SCCs?
[31:14] Jordan: we use standard SCCs where applicable and have DPA clauses for EU data residency. for right to be forgotten, we can surface process and remove persisted content upon request if it's stored in logs.

[33:40] David: can you confirm whether embeddings or KV cache content is stored in a way that could be reconstructed? we have HIPAA-adjacent concerns.
[33:52] Priya: embeddings may be cached for performance but we have options to disable persistent caching; for HIPAA-like use cases we recommend private deployment and strict key management.

[36:00] Jordan: let's recap next steps - i'll send the redline, dpa summary, and pricing workbook. priya will send the benchmarks and runbook. marta - you'll share procurement timeline and billing contact. david to share security checklist. we aim to reconvene after you review redlines.
[36:25] Marta: yes, we'll target review by next tuesday.

[38:10] Ethan: one more ops note - onboarding runbook includes a checklist: dns entries, vpc peering steps, k8s node sizing (if on-prem), and test plan. we'll tailor it for your infra.

[40:50] Sana: minor question - are there any model IP concerns if we fine-tune on our prompts?
[40:58] Jordan: customer retains outputs and derivative IP from fine-tuning; base model IP remains with the model provider. we'll document the standard language.

[44:00] Liam: procurement will likely push a SLA credit as a percent of monthly fees for each downtime incident. do you have standard credit formulas?
[44:12] Ethan: yes, we have a tiered credit schedule in the SLA - we'll include the exact table in the SLA draft.

[46:30] Marta: last thing - can you include a one-page summary of security artifacts for our vendor risk team?
[46:38] Jordan: yes - SOC2 report summary, ISO certs, subprocessors, KMS details, and sample audit logs extract. we'll attach as a single PDF.

[49:00] Jordan: alright thanks everyone, we'll get those artifacts to you by the dates we said. any final Qs?
[49:10] David: none from me.
[49:12] Sana: all good.
[49:15] Marta: thanks - looking forward to the redlines.

[52:00] Jordan: great, talk soon - bye everyone.

End of transcript.
